Table Function

Source: R/govTable.R
govTable.Rd

This function inserts a gov styled table. Format is with header looking rows and columns

Usage

govTable(
  inputId,
  df,
  caption,
  caption_size = "l",
  num_col = NULL,
  width_overwrite = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL
)

Arguments

inputId

The id assigned to the component's root element. For Shiny input components this is also the name used to access the value via input$<inputId>.

df

expects a dataframe to create a table

caption

The table's title, shown as its caption. Plain text is escaped and shown as written; use shiny::HTML() or tags for markup

caption_size

adjust the size of caption. One of "s", "m", "l", "xl", with "l" as the default. Any other value throws an error.

num_col

adds numeric class format to these columns

width_overwrite

change width. Need to include width for every column. Columns must add up to 1. Options are three-quarters, two-thirds, one-half, one-third, one-quarter. Default is NULL

subtitle

Optional line under the caption, in smaller, lighter text: what the data is, where and when it covers, and the units if every value shares them (e.g. "Cost of bikes (£), England, 2025"). It becomes part of the table's accessible name, with the caption. Needs a caption. Plain text is escaped and shown as written; use shiny::HTML() or tags for markup. NULL (default) shows no subtitle

Value

A div shiny tag holding the table, which has inputId as its id. Wide tables scroll sideways inside the div, not the whole page.

Details

For very large or interactive tables, consider govReactable() instead. govTable() renders a static HTML table, which becomes slow to render and harder to navigate as the number of rows grows. A warning is emitted when df has more than 50 rows.

Table titles

Every table needs a title. The Analysis Function guidance on tables suggests two parts, which match two arguments:

  • caption: a short headline stating the message, e.g. "Costs peaked in March".

  • subtitle: what the data is, where and when, e.g. "Cost of bikes, vans and buses (£), England, January to May 2025". Include the units if every value shares them.

A headline is optional. Without one, put the what, where and when in caption and leave out subtitle.

Put the source of the data under the table (for example with gov_text()), not in the title.

Screen reader users hear the caption and subtitle together when they reach the table, so keep them short and don't repeat information. See also the GOV.UK Design System table component.

See also

Other Govstyle tables tabs and accordions: accordion(), govReactable(), govReactable-shiny, govTabs(), update_reactable_caption()

Examples

ui <- shinyGovstyle::gov_page(
  shinyGovstyle::gov_main_layout(
    shinyGovstyle::govTable(
      "tab1",
      shinyGovstyle::transport_data_small,
      "Bike and car costs were highest in March",
      "l",
      num_col = c(2,3),
      width_overwrite = c("one-half", "one-quarter", "one-quarter"),
      subtitle = "Cost of bikes and cars, January to March"
    )
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {}

if (interactive()) shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
